symptom: `RETRIEVE $Rows FROM Mod.Item SORT BY System.createdDate ASC;` passed `mxcli check --references`, exec reported SUCCESS, and then mxbuild could not LOAD the project: `System.ArgumentNullException: Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'value') at Mendix.Modeler.DomainModels.Refs.AttributeRef.set_AttributeId` — an unhandled exception with a stack trace rather than a CE code, so Studio Pro cannot open it either (ako/CapTrackV3 FINDINGS §46).
cause: In addRetrieveAction the qualified-path branch validated `len(parts) >= 3` (Module.Entity.Attribute), so a TWO-part path fell through every check and was written verbatim as the sort's AttributeQualifiedName. `System.createdDate` reads as Module.Attribute and names no entity, so Mendix resolves it to nothing and stores a null AttributeId. Fixed by refusing a two-part sort path with a message naming the bare spelling that works. Refused rather than repaired: Module.Attribute has no reading that names an entity, and the two candidate repairs mean different things.
file: `mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_builder_actions.go` (the qualified branch of the SORT BY loop in addRetrieveAction); tests `mdl/executor/microflow_create_and_sort_test.go`; example `mdl-examples/bug-tests/create-output-variable-and-sort-path.mdl`
insight: The report said exec failed; exec SUCCEEDS — the .NET exception comes from `mx` reading the model afterwards, which is a different layer and changes where to look. This is also the severest outcome in this codebase's taxonomy (an unloadable project, the ADR-0005 class) reached from a script every mxcli gate accepted. The scope is narrower than the report implies, and the obvious reading is wrong: measured on 11.14.0, `sort by createdDate` on an entity that STORES it builds at 0 errors, and CE1613 on an entity that does not is Mendix being right, not a defect. An earlier conclusion here — that mxcli could not sort by a system member at all — came from testing against an entity without AutoCreatedDate, and was corrected only by re-measuring with it enabled. Ground truth for the stored shape came from grepping a Studio Pro-authored unit in the same project: `DomainModels$AttributeRef Attribute = "System.XASInstance.createdDate"`, i.e. always three parts.
